source.sourceLessonTitleEnglish: Keeping a Tired Crew Going Before Hotel Opening
source.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Encourage a tired crew, make concrete commitments on breaks and help, and talk with a young laborer about staying.

openDomainReview.question: Preserve the San Antonio hotel opening in two weeks, a month of overtime, carpenter lead Fernanda Ruiz, foreman Héctor Molina, door-frame mistakes and the project manager's approved extra lobby workers. Review burnout, overtime and morale terms and reported speech without changing the workers' accounts.

Keep Héctor's concrete commitments distinct: nobody works Sunday, two extra people arrive tomorrow, and the crew's effort is recognized. Qualified Japanese/workplace reviewers must settle plural crew address, register, home-stretch idiom and whether the draft's promise wording adds certainty beyond the source.

Iván Paredes is a 19-year-old laborer who plans to resign Friday because overtime without a raise does not cover rent and he is not learning new skills. Héctor offers to discuss training with the office, Monday carpentry work with Fernanda, and to ask the project manager for a raise. Iván agrees to stay at least until opening; no raise or training approval has yet occurred. Review employment terms and conditional promises with qualified Japanese/domain reviewers.

rows.sourceSpanish: Faltan 2 semanas para la fecha de apertura de un hotel en San Antonio, y la cuadrilla lleva un mes haciendo horas extra.
rows.sourceEnglish: There are 2 weeks left before the opening date of a hotel in San Antonio, and the crew has been working overtime for a month.

rows.sourceSpanish: En el lobby, Fernanda Ruiz, la líder de carpinteros, le dice al capataz Héctor Molina que el cansancio ya se nota en los marcos de las puertas.
rows.sourceEnglish: In the lobby, Fernanda Ruiz, the carpenter lead, tells foreman Héctor Molina that the tiredness is already showing in the door frames.

rows.sourceSpanish: Fernanda: Si seguimos así, el agotamiento nos va a costar más errores y más tiempo.
rows.sourceEnglish: Fernanda: If we keep going like this, the burnout is going to cost us more mistakes and more time.
rows.speaker: Fernanda

rows.sourceSpanish: Héctor: Fernanda, gracias por decírmelo; hablaré hoy con el gerente.
rows.sourceEnglish: Héctor: Fernanda, thanks for telling me; I'll talk to the manager today.
rows.speaker: Héctor
rows.conditionalJapanesePhrase: フェルナンダさん、教えてくれてありがとう。今日、マネージャーに話しておくね。

rows.sourceSpanish: Durante el almuerzo, Héctor llama al gerente del proyecto, y él aprueba personal adicional para terminar el lobby.
rows.sourceEnglish: During lunch, Héctor calls the project manager, and he approves extra workers to finish the lobby.

rows.sourceSpanish: A la hora de salida, Héctor reúne a la cuadrilla junto a la entrada porque el ánimo está muy bajo.
rows.sourceEnglish: At quitting time, Héctor gathers the crew by the entrance because morale is very low.

rows.sourceSpanish: Héctor: Sé que están cansados, y tienen razón.
rows.sourceEnglish: Héctor: I know you're tired, and you're right.
rows.speaker: Héctor
rows.conditionalJapanesePhrase: 皆さんが疲れているのは分かっています。皆さんの言うとおりです。

rows.sourceSpanish: Héctor: El domingo nadie trabajará; tendrán su día de descanso.
rows.sourceEnglish: Héctor: Nobody will work on Sunday; you'll get your day off.
rows.speaker: Héctor
rows.conditionalJapanesePhrase: 日曜日は誰も作業しません。皆さんには休日をきちんと取ってもらいます。

rows.sourceSpanish: Héctor: Mañana traeré 2 personas más para ayudar en el lobby.
rows.sourceEnglish: Héctor: Tomorrow I'll bring 2 more people to help in the lobby.
rows.speaker: Héctor
rows.conditionalJapanesePhrase: 明日、ロビーの応援にあと2人連れてきます。

rows.sourceSpanish: Héctor: Estamos en la recta final, y su esfuerzo ya se ve en cada piso del hotel.
rows.sourceEnglish: Héctor: We're in the home stretch, and your effort already shows on every floor of the hotel.
rows.speaker: Héctor

rows.sourceSpanish: Héctor: Vamos a lograrlo, y lo vamos a hacer bien.
rows.sourceEnglish: Héctor: We're going to make it, and we're going to do it right.
rows.speaker: Héctor
rows.conditionalJapanesePhrase: 間に合わせます。そして、きちんと仕上げます。

rows.sourceSpanish: Héctor: Confío en ustedes; han hecho un trabajo excelente.
rows.sourceEnglish: Héctor: I trust you all; you've done excellent work.
rows.speaker: Héctor
rows.conditionalJapanesePhrase: 皆さんを信頼しています。素晴らしい仕事をしてくれています。

rows.sourceSpanish: Después, Iván Paredes, un ayudante de 19 años, le dice a Héctor que piensa presentar su renuncia el viernes.
rows.sourceEnglish: Afterward, Iván Paredes, a 19-year-old laborer, tells Héctor that he plans to hand in his resignation on Friday.

rows.sourceSpanish: Héctor: Iván, ¿por qué estás pensando en irte?
rows.sourceEnglish: Héctor: Iván, why are you thinking about leaving?
rows.speaker: Héctor
rows.conditionalJapanesePhrase: イバンさん、どうして辞めようと思っているの？

rows.sourceSpanish: Iván: Hago muchas horas extra, pero sin un aumento no me alcanza para la renta y no aprendo nada nuevo.
rows.sourceEnglish: Iván: I work a lot of overtime, but without a raise I can't cover the rent and I'm not learning anything new.
rows.speaker: Iván

rows.sourceSpanish: Héctor: Si te quedas, hablaré con la oficina sobre tu capacitación.
rows.sourceEnglish: Héctor: If you stay, I'll talk to the office about your training.
rows.speaker: Héctor
rows.conditionalJapanesePhrase: 残ってくれるなら、研修のことを事務所に話すよ。

rows.sourceSpanish: Héctor: El lunes empezarás a trabajar con Fernanda en carpintería, y le pediré al gerente del proyecto un aumento para ti.
rows.sourceEnglish: Héctor: On Monday you'll start working with Fernanda in carpentry, and I'll ask the project manager for a raise for you.
rows.speaker: Héctor

rows.sourceSpanish: Iván sonríe y dice que se quedará por lo menos hasta la fecha de apertura.
rows.sourceEnglish: Iván smiles and says he'll stay at least until the opening date.
